preamble: Diphthongization of a mid front vowel /e/ to [ei] through development of a palatal off-glide. It is common in the history of European languages: Latin tonic ē in open syllables became Old French ei, and Icelandic diphthongized e before ng and nk.

examples.note: Tonic close-mid e in a free syllable diphthongized to ei (later oi: toile).
Early Old French and northern form; later mois.

examples.from: drengur 'boy' (/ɛ/ before ng; < Old Norse drengr)
examples.note: In the standard dialect /ɛ/ becomes [ei] before the nasals of ng and nk; Westfjords dialects keep the monophthong.
